qAndA.answer: Boiling chips provide nucleation sites to prevent superheating and bumping of the liquid during boiling. They ensure smooth and controlled boiling.
qAndA.question: What is the purpose of the boiling chips in the conical vial?

qAndA.answer: The thermometer is placed in the vapor path of the still head to measure the temperature of the distilling vapor, not the boiling liquid. This allows for accurate determination of the boiling point of the distillate.
qAndA.question: Why is the thermometer placed at the top of the still head, rather than in the conical vial?

qAndA.answer: Anhydrous sodium sulfate is a drying agent that absorbs any residual water present in the distillate, ensuring a pure and dry product.
qAndA.question: Why is anhydrous sodium sulfate added to the collected distillate?

qAndA.answer: The Hickman still head has a small collection area, allowing for efficient condensation and collection of distillate even with small volumes of liquid, making it suitable for microscale experiments.
qAndA.question: How does the Hickman still head facilitate microscale distillation?

text_to_speech: This video demonstrates how to perform a microscale distillation using a Hickman still head. The distillation apparatus includes a ring stand with one small clamp, a hot plate, an aluminum heating block, a clean and dry 5-mL conical vial with screw cap, boiling chips, a Hickman still head with a one-hole septum and screw cap, and a digital thermometer. Place the aluminum block on top of the hot plate. Place the 5-mL conical vial in one of the openings of the aluminum block. At this point, add 2 or 3 boiling chips to the conical vial. Then, add the reagents to the conical vial. In this particular case the reagents are 2-methylcyclohexanol and phosphoric acid. Concentrated acids are corrosive. Always wash hands after use. Attach the Hickman still head to the conical vial and lightly tighten the screw cap that secures the junction. Place the one-hole septum with Teflon-coating side down against the glass and tighten the screw cap on top of the still head. Attach a digital thermometer to the top of the still head. Suspend the thermometer with a clamp in order to measure the temperature of the vapor, rather than the liquid. Heat the reaction mixture to boiling. Note the temperature of the still head as you are collecting distillate. Keep the temperature of the distillation below 95°C. This mixture will need to be heated well in order for the distillate to reach the still head. You might need to set the hot plate to max to generate sufficient vapor. The material being collected will accumulate on the lip of the still head. DO NOT ALLOW THE DISTILLATION POT TO RUN DRY. This distillation is not quantitative (that means that you won’t collect all of the product that is made, just a sample of it). Turn off the heat and lift the whole apparatus from the aluminum block to let it cool off. Using a long-stemmed Pasteur Pipet, transfer the liquid accumulated on the lip of the still head to a clean test tube. Add a small amount of anhydrous sodium sulfate and let it dry for 2 minutes. Carefully transfer the dried liquid to a clean test tube.
